title: Topological Tricritical Ising Universality Class in One Dimension
authors: Sheng Yang, Hai-Qing Lin, Xue-Jia Yu
abstract: Recent advances have revealed that quantum critical universality can be enriched by nontrivial topology. Here we study the tricritical point of the one-dimensional cluster O Brien-Fendley model and show that it realizes a topologically nontrivial tricritical Ising ($\text{TCI}^*$) universality class. The transition shares the local bulk conformal data of ordinary TCI criticality, while realizing a distinct symmetry-enriched topological sector, manifested through a protected twofold degeneracy under open boundary conditions. We further show that TCI criticality admits two spontaneously fixed boundary conditions, realized respectively through symmetry enrichment and boundary renormalization-group flow, which are distinguished by the $\mathbb{Z}_2^T$ charge of the disorder field. Remarkably, we find that the topological twofold degeneracy at the $\text{TCI}^*$ critical point exhibits an exponential energy splitting, in stark contrast to the algebraic splitting at the $\text{Ising}^*$ critical point. These results reveal a symmetry-enriched form of TCI criticality and uncover topologically distinct boundary structures beyond those of the ordinary TCI theory.
summary: This work explores novel quantum critical points by studying the cluster O’Brien–Fendley model. The authors establish a distinct $	ext{TCI}^*$ universality class characterized by unique boundary physics and an exponential energy splitting of its topological edge modes. This research advances the understanding of how topology enriches criticality in low-dimensional quantum systems.
main_problem: To investigate whether a topologically distinct Tricritical Ising (TCI) universality class ($	ext{TCI}^*$) exists beyond the ordinary TCI criticality, particularly concerning topological aspects at quantum critical points.
main_result: The $	ext{TCI}^*$ QCP exhibits a twofold topological degeneracy with an exponential energy splitting, distinguishing it from the ordinary TCI point and revealing distinct boundary structures.
method: The study employs field-theoretic analysis, large-scale numerical simulations (DMRG), and Conformal Boundary Field Theory (BCFT) techniques to analyze critical exponents and low-energy spectra.
model_or_system: The system is based on the cluster O’Brien–Fendley (OF) model, a spin-1/2 chain with multiple three-body interactions, analyzed near its tricritical point ($g_c \approx 0.428$).
key_observables: Central charge ($c$), boundary magnetization ($m_{bdy}$), boundary correlation exponent ($\Delta_{s\sigma}$), and the energy splitting ($\Delta E$) of edge modes.
important_parameters: Tuning parameter $g$, critical coupling constants, and system size $L$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the low-energy physics to established CFT/BCFT frameworks for comparison.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate finite-size scaling of correlation functions ($\Delta_{s\sigma}$), comparisons of low-energy spectra under different boundary conditions, and plots showing exponential decay of energy splitting at $	ext{TCI}^*$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the critical behavior of the cluster OF model to ordinary TCI theory by analyzing boundary correlation functions, confirming distinct scaling dimensions ($\Delta_{s\sigma}$), and demonstrating the unique exponential energy splitting characteristic of the $	ext{TCI}^*$ point.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous theoretical framework for identifying symmetry-enriched topological phases beyond standard critical theories, which is highly relevant to modern condensed matter theory.
